To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HPV18 seropositivty rates after HPV vaccination in HIV-infected young woman remained high at week 48 after vaccination as measured by IgG LIA, in contrast with cLIA.

We compared antibody (Ab) responses to human papillomaviruses (HPV) type 6, 16, 18 and 11 in HIV-infected young adult women using total immunoglobulins (Ig)G Luminex immuoassay and competitive Luminx immunoassay.

HPV vaccine is immunogenic and safe among HIV-infected young adult women, and that the lower rate (73%) of seroposivity to HPV18 measured with cLIIA vs. 98% measured with IgGIA is due to the assay and not due to immunologic factors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immune response to the HPV vaccine in HIV infected young women, and the development of a more sensitive assay for measuring the immune response.
understanding the immune system and its role in the development of vaccines.
the development of new technologies for the analysis and characterization of the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cLIA assay does not measure the same thing as the IgG LIA assay and that the cLIIA assay is less sensitive than the IgG LIIA assay.

both assays can be used to measure antibody responses to quadrivalent HPV vaccine in HIV-infected young adult women, with cLIA providing additional information regarding the relative avidity of antibodies.
the cLIA assay is less sensitive than the IgG LIA assay for measuring antibody responses to HPV18.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found no evidence of reduced immunogenicity of the HPV vaccine in HIV-positive women, as measured by antibody responses to HPV6, HPV11, HPV16, and HPV18.
the HPV vaccine was immunogenic in HIV-infected women, and the antibody responses were durable for all vaccine HPV types.

the competitive Luminex assay may underestimate antibody levels to HPV-18 in the presence of anti-human antibodies, and that the total IgG Luminex assay is more reliable for measuring HPV-18 antibody responses in HIV-infected women.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cLIA assay should be used with caution in HIV-infected individuals.
the cLIA is a more sensitive assay than the IgG LIA for measuring seropositivity, but the cLIA assay is more expensive than the IgG assay.
the cLIA assay is not a good measure of HPV18 antibody responses.
